claim: A retrospective study analyzes 56.7 million Waymo rider-only miles through January 2025 and reports lower crash rates than matched human benchmarks for the examined aggregate injury outcomes.
source_or_reference: Kusano et al., Comparison of Waymo Rider-Only Crash Rates by Crash Type to Human Benchmarks at 56.7 Million Miles. https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.01515
evidence_type: Original research abstract; developer-authored observational analysis
notes: Supports bounded driverless capability and safety evidence; not every operator, geography, condition, or current software version. Full methods not audited in this draft.

claim: Recall 25E-034 documents collisions involving chains and gates; the affected fleet received updated software.
source_or_reference: Waymo manufacturer submission hosted by NHTSA, Part 573 Safety Recall Report 25E-034. https://static.nhtsa.gov/odi/rcl/2025/RCLRPT-25E034-2471.PDF
evidence_type: Original manufacturer recall filing in regulator archive
notes: Demonstrates specific historical failure modes and remediation; not proof of an unresolved defect today or an exhaustive current recall inventory.

claim: NHTSA distinguishes ADS from Level 2 assistance and cautions about interpreting crash data, including exposure differences.
source_or_reference: NHTSA Standing General Order on Crash Reporting. https://www.nhtsa.gov/laws-regulations/standing-general-order-crash-reporting
notes: Use comparable exposure and ODD evidence; raw crash totals cannot rank safety.

claim: The CPUC authorizes drivered and driverless passenger service programs and publishes quarterly reporting requirements.
source_or_reference: CPUC Autonomous Vehicle Programs and AV Program Quarterly Reporting. https://www.cpuc.ca.gov/regulatory-services/licensing/transportation-licensing-and-analysis-branch/autonomous-vehicle-programs/
date_or_recency: Program page and reporting search results inspected 2026-10-22
notes: Supports existence of regulated service programs. No permit-level or trip-data audit performed; does not establish permission for these hypothetical cases.

claim: Waymo publicly offers autonomous ride-hailing service in selected service areas.
notes: Supports existing commercial service; not proof of coverage, partnership availability or approval for the hypothetical organization.

claim: Tesla describes Cybercab as having no steering wheel, accelerator pedal or brake pedal.
date_or_recency: Official overview retrieved in search on 2026-10-23
notes: Illustrates artifact-level reliance on automation, not societal irreversibility or independently verified universal capability.
